description: Append-only queue of flag-don't-fix / deferred decisions. New entries are appended; existing entries are never mutated in place.

queue.rationale: A clean uninstall inverse is impossible without a generation-time pre-image/backup, which would be a RUNTIME change out of SP-8's no-behavior-change scope — merge-action hooks in a possibly-preexisting settings.json can't be safely un-merged; add-header/modernize mutate files in place with no saved pre-image; origin:adopted artifacts must never be touched; seed-if-absent docs may be user-edited.
queue.resolution: Deferred to a possible future minor (a new skill + 3 doc inventories + a skill-count test, not a patch). Recorded as an onboard 3.1.1 breadcrumb in onboard/CHANGELOG.md so the decision is durable and visible in the PR.

queue.title: Wave-4 candidate (SP-11+) — close the 'gate that cannot fail' class across onboard's test/gate surface
queue.rationale: Three P5 review rounds each fixed instances of one failure mode — a gate/fixture/belt that reports success without exercising what it claims — and each fix left the class alive one file over. Deferred as a dedicated hardening sprint rather than chased instance-by-instance inside the diet, per developer decision at the round-3 gate. NONE breaks shipped behavior; all are latent guard gaps.
items: R3-SP8-01: check-ref-paths.sh's .json coverage is unfalsifiable — tests/ref-paths/test-check-ref-paths.sh has no .json arm; reverting the feature leaves all belts green. Add resolving/dangling .json fixtures; assert BROKEN count.

R3-RISK-1 / CORR-F1: check-ref-paths.sh reports an unearned pass on a missing ROOT (sibling check-phase-numbering.sh got the guard this round; this one didn't). Also its root-relative branch is CWD-relative and exempts the 4 research-schema .json refs it was added for. Add the -e ROOT guard; convert the 4 to citing-file-relative or a named exemption list.

R3-SP8-03: the lookalike exemption swallows a dangling .json whose basename is absent under onboard/ — catches a RELOCATION but not a RENAME/TYPO. Make onboard/schemas/*.json refs non-exemptible, or allowlist the generated-into-target basenames.

R3-SP8-04: the numbering self-test derives its per-violation list from the fixture, so gutting bad-steps.md to 1 line keeps the belt green (55->46 ok, no FAIL). Pin the expected violation count per fixture.

R3-CORR-F2 / TEST-1: the schema parity belt asserts 'byte-identical accept/reject' but checks only required[]/additionalProperties — 6 malformed shapes flip ACCEPT->REJECT invisibly. Replace with a real HEAD-vs-new differential over an instance corpus; add named-key reject fixtures.

R3-RISK-2: the restored Research self-audit (and start's prose generally) is pinned only by the CI-excluded release-gate; every belt guard on start/SKILL.md is a don't-grow ratchet. Add a must_present_nonempty verbatim pin (the pattern already used for generate's 5 safety strings).
R3-SP8-06 / CORR-F5: check-phase-numbering.sh reports a pass over an existing-but-empty ROOT (zero .md files). Count scanned files; fail on zero.
R3-CORR-F4: unspaced em-dash (**Step 8—Verify**) false-flags an in-family label. Strip trailing em-dash-and-beyond before shaping.
R3-CORR-F7: indented headings and paren-delimited ordered lists evade declaration detection. Allow ^[[:space:]]{0,3}#{1,6} and [0-9]+[.)].
R3-TEST-2: the ordered-list declaration form has only positive coverage; add an ordered-list violation to bad-steps.md.
R3-PRIN-1: the belt re-asserts ref integrity the dedicated CI job already owns (belt:98-102) — duplicate assertion site the belt's own header disclaims. Delete it.

release-gate: run-automated-checks.sh is excluded from run-all.sh discovery, so it caught a dropped instruction CI could not (U6). It also hardcodes versions (drifts each sprint) and launders check-schemas exit 2 as a warning. Make it CI-discoverable, derive its version pins from plugin.json, and bring its exit-2 to parity with the belt's hard-fail.

queue.title: matali reads lens:engine return/input fields lens declares nowhere (agents roster, modelPolicy)
queue.rationale: SP-10's new single declared programmatic surface (lens/skills/engine/references/engine-api.md) records an `agents` finder roster as an explicitly non-contracted consumer assumption, but the same cross-repo pass surfaced a second, undocumented divergence in the opposite direction (`modelPolicy`, sent by matali but never consumed or acknowledged by lens). Neither breaks anything today — lens ignores unknown input fields and consumers are told to default `agents` to [] — but both are truth gaps between the two repos that a future lens contract change could silently break for matali. Resolve in the matali repo (stop depending on undeclared fields) or via a future lens contract addition (declare and honor them explicitly).
items: matali plugin `skills/review/SKILL.md:186,216` and `CLAUDE.md:52` read an `agents` finder roster off the `lens:engine` return; lens declares this nowhere in its schema or in engine-api.md's returns section — it is recorded only under engine-api.md's '## Known consumer assumptions (not part of the contract)'.

matali also passes `modelPolicy` as an argument to `lens:engine`; engine-api.md's '## lens:engine — inputs' section does not list it as a consumed input at all — a second, undocumented consumer-side divergence (matali sending something lens never reads).

queue.title: SP-10 exit-gate deferrals: CI ref-guard scope, stale site, reconcile.md framing, unretargeted belts
queue.rationale: Four items surfaced at the SP-10 exit gate that are correctly out of this diet's bounded scope — three are floor-protected or shared-gate concerns needing a dedicated pass, one is deferred release housekeeping. The CI ref-guard scoping defect is the lens-side instance of the same 'gate that cannot fail' class already tracked under SP11-guard-hardening (onboard's check-ref-paths/check-skill-refs surface): SP-10 fixed it locally in-belt (tests/lens/test_engine_api.sh invokes both guards with the explicit `lens` argument, permanently), but did not fix the CI-workflow root cause, since loosening a shared onboard gate repo-wide is out of scope for a lens diet.
items: CI ref-guard scoping defect: `.github/workflows/validate.yml:104,106` invokes check-skill-refs.sh / check-ref-paths.sh with no argument, so ROOT defaults to `onboard` and every other plugin (including lens) is ungated in CI — the lens belt is the only durable coverage. Additionally check-skill-refs.sh:20 resolves `<path>/SKILL.md` tokens from the citing file's dir only (no repo-root fallback, no code-fence awareness), which produced 7 false positives on lens during SP-10 — same guard-defect class as SP11-guard-hardening's onboard-side findings.
Stale site: site/index.html:221 still pins lens v1.4.1 and site/lens/index.html is stale after the 1.4.3 bump; site regeneration is deferred to the combined develop->main release.

reconcile.md:110 framing is now slightly stale post-retirement of lens:review's orchestrator mode: it says the compute-only mode applies 'When lens is driven by an orchestrator ... instead of a human running /lens:review', but post-retirement the orchestrator drives lens:engine and lens:render-review directly, and it is render-review's Step 1 that runs reconcile compute-only. Not fixed in SP-10 because floor (a) mandates reconcile.md stay zero-diff.

Five belts were not retargeted to the new engine-api.md canon and still pin prose in the demoted files: test_injected_intent.sh, test_injected_finders.sh, test_intent_fencing.sh, test_multi_spec.sh, test_doc_contracts.sh. Deferred to keep the SP-10 diff bounded; none pin a literal type block so they remain accurate, just not canon-sourced.

queue.title: Both repo reference guards report success without checking anything, in two distinct ways
queue.rationale: Filed as its own entry rather than appended to SP10-exit-gate-deferred, because this queue's contract (see the top-level description) is that existing entries are never mutated in place. Same family as SP11-guard-hardening's 'gate that cannot fail' class. Both defects were demonstrated, not inferred.
items: Guard vacuous-pass: .github/scripts/check-ref-paths.sh exits 0 after find(1) errors when given a bad ROOT (e.g. `check-ref-paths.sh nosuchplugin` prints the success line and exits 0), so a typo'd plugin name is indistinguishable from a clean tree and yields a silent green. Found during SP-10 P4 VERIFY while proving the guards non-vacuous. Same family as the SP11-guard-hardening 'gate that cannot fail' class.

check-skill-refs.sh has the identical bad-ROOT defect: `check-skill-refs.sh lenz` prints 'find: lenz: No such file or directory' followed by 'skill-refs: all <path>/SKILL.md references resolve' and exits 0. Only the check-ref-paths half was previously queued.

BOTH guards wrap per-file extraction in `grep ... 2>/dev/null` inside a process substitution, so a file the guard cannot read contributes zero refs AND zero errors. Demonstrated: plant a dangling 'nope/SKILL.md' ref, chmod 000 the file -> both guards exit 0; chmod 644 -> BROKEN reported. Fix: capture find's status, assert scanned>0, drop 2>/dev/null, and count a grep exit >=2 as broken.

check-ref-paths.sh:48-53 exempts any ref whose basename does not exist under ROOT, so a citation to a wholly nonexistent file (./no-such-file.md) passes silently. The relocation class IS caught; the typo class is not.

queue.title: lens 1.4.3 adds a third render-review return (`noop:`) that matali does not yet know
queue.rationale: lens 1.4.3's empty-scope short-circuit now returns the line `noop: nothing to review` (a success, no artifact) instead of answering on `skipped:`, which lens declares as its failure-only channel. matali, the live consumer, branches only on `wrote:` vs `skipped:` and knows nothing about `noop:`, so today an empty scope still reads as a render failure there. Nothing breaks -- matali's `skipped:` handling is already degrade-not-block -- but until matali learns `noop:`, an ordinary empty-diff phase is reported as a degrade. Cross-repo: cannot be fixed from claude-plugins.
items: matali `references/delegation-contract.md:54` maps a `skipped:` return to 'render no doc this phase, warn once' -- it should treat `noop: nothing to review` as a clean no-op (no doc, no warning) and keep the warn path for `skipped:` alone.
matali `skills/pipeline/SKILL.md:665` maps a `skipped:` return to 'Degrade (R10) => no link, note' -- same split needed, so an empty scope stops being counted as a degrade.
Contract source of truth for the three returns: lens `skills/engine/references/engine-api.md` section '## lens:render-review -- inputs and returns' and `skills/render-review/SKILL.md` Step 4.
queue.note: Appended as a new entry (never mutating an existing one) per this queue's top-level contract. Resolve in the matali repo.

queue.title: SP-10 P5 REVIEW findings accepted as deferred at the gate (13 conformance + 3 advisory merit)
queue.rationale: Ten independent eyes produced 26 findings. At the P5 gate the developer chose to fix C1 (the emptyScope failure-channel defect) and C2-C7/C10 (the mutation-proven belt holes); C11 was fixed separately as an orchestration error. These are the remainder — real, verified, and consciously deferred rather than silently dropped. None blocks the release; several are cheap and would suit a Wave-4 pass alongside SP11-guard-hardening.
items: C8 engine-api.md contradicts itself: the Ownership map marks `target`/`finders` required (no `?`) while the prose 11 lines later says 'every one is optional'; and it says every input arrives via the Skill-tool channel while the `finders` row says it is read from .claude/lens/settings.md. The runtime is genuinely split too (review/SKILL.md:26 vs finder-registry.md:63).

C9 engine-api.md:110 calls recommendedEscalation 'the max surviving severity', but severity is critical|high|medium|low and escalation is minor|moderate|major|critical. Only `critical` maps to itself; pipeline.md §6 holds the real mapping. A caller implementing it literally is wrong for 3 of 4 values.

C12 The 1.4.3 CHANGELOG entry body is unpinned; sibling belts awk-scope their own version blocks (test_injected_finders for 1.3.0, test_intent_fencing:37 for 1.2.0). SP-10 skipped its own, and 1.4.3 carries the only disclosure of the emptyScope behavior change.

C13 'The four field-enumeration bullets are gone' guards only three: re-materializing '- **`dimension` enum:**' in lens/CLAUDE.md matches neither negative pin. Highest drift risk of the four, since the dimension enum is co-owned across two repos.

C14 markdown-fallback.md got the same example-path edit as the six lens/agents files but is excluded from the JSON-integrity guard (its fences are ```markdown, not ```json). Seven files edited, six guarded. Its nested 4-backtick/3-backtick fence has no integrity check at all.

C15 tests/lens/test_render_review.sh:39-42 duplicates :11/:16 byte-for-byte with a rationale that cannot hold (two identical greps over one file cannot diverge); :34 is subsumed by the whole-line heading pin at :50/:53.

C16 engine-api.md hardcodes matali's line numbers (SKILL.md 186/216, plugin CLAUDE.md 52) in what is now the canonical contract. Accurate today; no guard here can hold them true. Cite by stable anchor instead.

C17 Unresolvable process identifiers in shipped test comments ('criterion 15a/15b/16', "U3's gatekeeper", 'Floor (b)'). The repo's SP-N convention is fine (six precedents cite durable repo-resident lessons); these point at run-scoped artifacts under docs/, which .gitignore excludes wholesale.

C18 Three belt assertions duplicate test_doc_contracts.sh:54,65,66 exactly ('4 engine stages', 'schema-parity target', 'live consumer'); :409-413 overlap its DERIVED skill-list check at :38-41, which is the better guard. Note the fencing pins at :19-22 are NOT duplicates and must stay.

C19 The canon elects `target` canonical while pipeline.md §2/§3, matali's call site and engine/SKILL.md all use `scope` — engine/SKILL.md never names `target`. A caller reading the single declared surface writes the spelling the runtime never mentions.

C20 tests/lens/test_engine_api.sh bundles five concerns in one file and prints PASS four times before finishing, so a real failure renders as 'PASS...PASS...PASS...PASS...FAIL'. The other 12 lens belts are 22-74 lines, one concern each.

C21 The example-path repairs are half-finished: risk-classify.md:51 pairs '"path": "src/api/handlers.ts"' with '"note": "Changes the /lens:review entrypoint contract"'; correctness.md:49 attributes a walkthrough:render error to a generic API handler. Few-shot exemplars that contradict themselves.

C22/C23 engine-api.md never states that an undeclared input arg is ignored rather than rejected (matali already depends on this for modelPolicy); and the Ownership map's Owner column - the file's core deliverable - is pinned only at heading level.

MERIT (advisory, 3/3 judges): over-engineering - a 424-line belt guards a 122-line doc, of which only ~15 lines are consolidated shapes; completeness - lens/CLAUDE.md:50 and :155 still restate the surface, so it did not become 'a true index' as the ask required; architecture - a live runtime behavior change shipped inside a doc-consolidation phase on a patch bump. Judges recommended cutting the belt toward 100 lines and splitting the behavior change into its own minor.

PRE-EXISTING, surfaced by merit: lens/CLAUDE.md:140 says 'the engine compares the new findings against the prior set ... and tracks the severity trend', but CLAUDE.md:37/:153 and the new canon all say the engine has 4 stages and reconcile owns that. Not introduced by this diff; contradicts the canon it now points at.
